candidates: [TECH] When assessing images with high-contrast lighting or strong artificial illumination, do not equate vividness or sharpness with higher quality; instead, evaluate whether the lighting enhances or detracts from perceived realism.
[AESTH] When an image contains a dominant color or texture pattern, do not score it higher solely for its vibrancy; instead, consider whether the composition feels balanced and visually pleasing.
[CONTENT] When evaluating scenes with human subjects or animals, do not overlook contextual clarity; instead, ensure facial expressions, actions, and interactions are discernible and coherent.
[NATURAL] When judging images with low-light or night scenes, do not reward glow or luminance alone; instead, assess whether the scene appears natural or unnaturally enhanced.

[GLOBAL] When scoring any image, do not rely on isolated dimension scores without considering overall impression; instead, integrate technical, aesthetic, and content factors into a holistic judgment.
